_purpose: The vocabulary of what mcgyvr can be asked to do. Each entry states what accepting it promises (`guarantee`), which family of the ladder it may start on (`starts_on`), which use case it belongs to (`use_case`), and what evidence a contract of that type must carry (`required_evidence`). `task_types` is the whole vocabulary: `code`, `chat`, `agent` and `media`. `deterministic_operations` are not task types: each names the task type a contract asks for it under (`task_type: code` with `operation: <name>`), and the product runs it with a tool, never a model. This file is the only definition: adding a task type is an edit here, not a code change.

vendored_from._note: The starting vocabulary was inherited from local-ai's triage map. It was inherited, not validated.

families.name: deterministic
families.doc: Tools. A program executes the change; no model is asked and no tokens are spent. Exactly one attempt, because a tool fails identically on retry.

families.name: local
families.doc: Models served by a source needing no credential. The keyless install runs here with the deterministic gate as its whole acceptance bar.

families.name: api
families.doc: Models served by a source needing a credential. The dearest family, and the one the north star measures spend against.

_families_note: Ordered cheapest to dearest. A family is the ladder-independent way to say where work starts: rung names are chosen by whoever wrote the config, so a catalog that named rungs would only be valid on the machine it was written for. A family resolves against any ladder — a rung is `api` when its unit declares an `api_key_env` and `local` when it does not.

use_cases.name: coding
use_cases.doc: Scoped edits to a repository, judged by a deterministic gate over code.

use_cases.name: chat
use_cases.doc: Raw prompt-to-response over a bound fleet; no gate, an endpoint for a harness.

use_cases.name: agent
use_cases.doc: Personal-assistant tasks over the repository files a contract names as its `sources`, answered in plain prose and ungated like chat; the backend is llama.cpp / vLLM with tool-calling, a serving-layer capability rather than a gate rung.

use_cases.name: media-gen
use_cases.doc: Image, video and speech generation, judged by media-valid, safety and ASR gates.

evidence_kinds.name: gate
evidence_kinds.doc: The deterministic acceptance gate. The floor under every `code` contract; chat and agent are ungated, and media is judged by its own structural evidence through the gate's output-checks rung.

evidence_kinds.name: tool_idempotent
evidence_kinds.doc: Re-running the tool that produced the change produces no further change. Available only to the deterministic family, where a tool owns the output.

evidence_kinds.name: references_resolved
evidence_kinds.doc: Every reference the index resolved was updated. What the index could not resolve — dynamic access, reflection, strings — is reported as unhandled rather than assumed absent.

evidence_kinds.name: no_semantic_change
evidence_kinds.doc: The parsed structure is unchanged apart from the region the type is allowed to touch. A structural check, so the gate can judge it without running anything.

evidence_kinds.name: type_check
evidence_kinds.doc: The project's type checker passes on the changed target.

evidence_kinds.name: tests_pass
evidence_kinds.doc: The contract's acceptance commands pass in the sandbox.

evidence_kinds.name: failing_test_first
evidence_kinds.doc: An acceptance command that demonstrates the defect — it must fail before the change and pass after. Without it a fix is indistinguishable from a plausible edit. Carried in the contract's `demonstration` list, not `acceptance`: the two lists have opposite baseline expectations, and one flat list cannot say which command is which (#183).

evidence_kinds.name: media_valid
evidence_kinds.doc: The output artifact is a valid file of the declared media kind — correct format, dimensions or duration. A structural check the gate makes itself, so it needs no contract command.

evidence_kinds.name: safety_pass
evidence_kinds.doc: A deterministic safety classifier passes on the output. One kind serves media and text outputs alike — the gate runs it, the contract does not.

evidence_kinds.name: asr_wer
evidence_kinds.doc: An ASR pass transcribes the audio output and its word-error-rate against the transcript stays under the contract's threshold. The transcript is the contract's own target, so the gate judges it without a human.

_evidence_note: `baseline` states what the evidence's commands must do on the unchanged tree — `pass` for a regression signal, `fail` for a demonstration — and is only meaningful where `needs_commands` is true. It is data here rather than a rule in code so that the contract loader can check each command-needing kind against the right contract list (`acceptance` for pass, `demonstration` for fail) without naming any evidence kind (#183).

deterministic_operations.name: format
deterministic_operations.guarantee: The target is byte-identical to what the project's own formatter produces. No semantic change, and nothing is decided that the formatter's configuration did not already decide.
deterministic_operations.warrant: structural — the project's formatter is the definition of the correct output, so there is nothing for a model to be better at.
deterministic_operations.doc: Reformat existing code with the project's own formatter.

deterministic_operations.name: import_sort
deterministic_operations.guarantee: Imports are ordered as the project's own tool orders them, with no other change to the file.
deterministic_operations.warrant: structural — same argument as `format`; the tool's configuration is the specification.
deterministic_operations.doc: Order imports with the project's own tool.

deterministic_operations.name: lint_fix
deterministic_operations.guarantee: Every autofix the project's linter applies is applied, and nothing else is. A diagnostic the linter will not fix itself is explicitly out of scope for this operation rather than handed to a model under the same name.
deterministic_operations.warrant: structural — the linter decides both what is wrong and what the fix is.
deterministic_operations.doc: Apply the project linter's own autofixes.

deterministic_operations.name: rename_symbol
deterministic_operations.guarantee: Every reference the index resolved is renamed, across every file that holds one. References the index could not resolve are reported, not silently left behind.
deterministic_operations.warrant: structural — the index (#47) already resolved the references, so this fans across files without a model. It is the only multi-file operation in the catalog, and it is deterministic for exactly that reason.
deterministic_operations.doc: Rename a symbol across the files that reference it.

task_types.name: code
task_types.guarantee: A scoped change to one target, judged by the deterministic gate. Which checks back the judgement is derived from the contract itself: a `demonstration` adds `failing_test_first`, an `acceptance` adds `tests_pass`, `no_semantic_change: true` adds `no_semantic_change`, and `type_check: true` adds `type_check`; the gate is always the floor. With `operation:` set, the named deterministic operation does the work with a tool, and its own guarantee and evidence apply instead.
task_types.warrant: One type for every coding task. Kinds of coding work that differed only in which evidence the contract had to carry are one type whose evidence is derived from the contract's fields, so the model states relevance and the orthogonal flags rather than choosing among near-duplicates. Work a tool does outright is the same type with an `operation`, because what differs is who does the work, not what kind of work it is.
task_types.doc: Make a scoped edit to one named target. The gate judges the change, and the contract's own fields decide which checks back the judgement; with `operation:` a tool makes the change instead of a model.

task_types.name: chat
task_types.guarantee: The reply is the answer. Nothing judges it — chat is a raw prompt-to-response endpoint, and whether the answer is right is the harness's question, not the gate's.
task_types.warrant: There is no bar to clear — chat is a raw endpoint, so nothing is spent judging and the reply is served straight back.
task_types.doc: Answer a prompt directly, ungated. The raw endpoint of the chat use case.

task_types.name: agent
task_types.guarantee: The reply is the answer, worked from the contract's `sources`, which the worker is given numbered and whole. Nothing judges it — like chat, agent is ungated, and whether the answer is right is the harness's question, not the gate's.
task_types.warrant: There is no bar to clear (owner, e2e run 2 R11: agent and chat have no gates) — the reply is served straight back, and what makes it worth having is the sources the worker is given, not a check after it answers.
task_types.doc: Answer a prompt in plain prose from the repository files the contract names as its sources, ungated.

task_types.name: media
task_types.guarantee: The artifact at the target is a valid file of the contract's `media_kind` — the right format, with dimensions or a duration that can be read and are positive. Nothing else judges it.
task_types.warrant: structural — media_valid reads the artifact's own header and structure, so a wrong-kind, empty or truncated output is caught without a contract command.
task_types.doc: Generate one image, audio or video artifact, judged by the gate's media_valid check.
